semis.why: SOXX +0.93% pre already in the ref; Thursday's chipmaker bounce ran on 0.90x volume (NVDA 0.82x, AVGO 0.78x) while the conviction sits in memory (Hynix +5.4% on 1.79x, Samsung +3.4%), which SOXX barely weights; quad witching; nothing beyond the gap argues for extension

big_tech.why: NQ leading ES (+0.47 vs +0.19), Thursday's rebound came on 1.25x QQQ volume vs semis' 0.90x, and a third day of oil easing is a duration bid; but cluster +7.7% above the 50d with META rsi 74, so no adding

ai_power_infra.why: graded vs SOXX so same bet as semis; Infineon +2.4% / Aixtron +2.6% are real regular-session prints from -10% below the 50d (rebound, not extension) but Bloom is +24.6% above its 50d - bimodal cluster, no cluster-level edge beyond the gap

sg_banks.why: banks -0.17% on 1.45x volume today with OCBC 2.82x - third-Friday index-rebalance flow, not a signal; STI drift (-0.70% 5d) vs a Monday close that will mostly follow Friday's US tape, on which I am neutral

market.why: SPY flat pre (-0.06%, ES +0.19%); day-2 post-hike rebound, oil relief and quad-witching pinning pull against each other; industrial production 21:15 SGT + Fed speakers are second-order

summary.bottom_line: Hold. Don't add to big tech or chips today: this is day two of a post-Fed relief bounce, the gap is already in the price, and quad witching adds noise on top.
summary.where_we_are: 19:15 SGT / 07:15 ET Friday. US pre-market; SGX closed (STI -0.25%). Next: US industrial production 21:15 SGT, Fed speakers through the session, and the quarterly options-and-futures expiry (quad witching) into the 04:00 SGT Saturday close. No 20:30 SGT data release today.
summary.macro_attribution: Oil is the biggest mover since the last regular close: WTI down a third day, about -2% to roughly $100 (CNBC, Sep 18) - the tape's -5.6% print is a futures contract-roll artifact, not the move. The 10-year eased to 4.95% (tape, Thu close) and the VIX sits at 15.3, calm. The big-tech lean depends on oil and yields staying down; the chip lean does not.
what_happened: Stocks bounced Thursday, a day after the Fed's quarter-point hike and hint of one more knocked them down (CNBC, Sep 17). S&P and Nasdaq volume ran 1.17x and 1.25x normal on the bounce, chips (SOXX) only 0.90x (tape): big tech's rebound had conviction, the chipmakers' did not.

Oil fell a third day as Saudi Arabia routes extra cargoes around the attacked East-West pipeline via ship-to-ship transfers off Oman; WTI briefly broke below $100 (CNBC, Sep 18). Nasdaq futures lead, +0.47% vs S&P +0.19% (tape), as inflation worries ease (Reuters via Investing.com, Sep 18 05:14 ET).

Memory surged in Asia on real volume: SK Hynix +5.4% on 1.79x normal, Samsung +3.4%; KOSPI +2.66%, Taiwan +1.75% (tape, Fri close). No company-specific news found - this is the AI-chip trade relieved by oil and yields, not a print.

Bank of Japan hiked to 1.25%, a 31-year high, on a 7-2 split - and Japanese stocks rose while the yen and bond yields fell (CNBC, Sep 18): the market read the split vote as the end of the hiking run. Nikkei +1.72% (tape).
Pre-market: chips +0.93% (SOXX), big tech +0.45% (QQQ), S&P flat (tape) - thin, no volume behind it. Quad witching inflates volume and can swing the last hour without meaning anything.

per_group.semis: flat - the +0.9% gap is already in the price; the conviction is in memory (Hynix, Samsung, Micron +1.1% pre-market), which SOXX barely carries, while the chipmakers proper (Nvidia +0.6%, Broadcom +1.0%, TSMC flat pre-market) bounced Thursday on low volume. Beyond the gap I have nothing that argues for extension, so I'm not leaning.
per_group.big_tech: slightly up - Nasdaq futures lead, Thursday's bounce came on above-average volume, and a third day of oil easing is a bid for the longest-duration names. But the group sits 7.7% above its 50-day average with Meta's RSI at 74, so this is not an entry.
per_group.ai_power_infra: flat - the power semiconductors are rebounding from 10% below their 50-day (Infineon +2.4%, Aixtron +2.6% in Frankfurt's regular session - a rebound, not a stretch) but Bloom, the fuel-cell name, is 25% above its own; graded against the chip index this is the same bet as chips.
per_group.sg_banks: flat - banks -0.17% today on 1.45x volume with OCBC at 2.82x, which is third-Friday index-rebalance flow rather than selling; Monday's STI will mostly follow tonight's US close, on which I'm neutral.
per_group.market: flat - day-two relief and cheaper oil pull one way, expiry pinning and post-hike Fed speakers the other.

change_my_mind: SOXX holds its gap through the first hour on above-average volume: the memory bid is spreading to the chipmakers, and chips flips to slightly up.
WTI back above $102 (the Saudi workaround fails) or the 10-year back above 5.00%: the oil-and-yield relief breaks, and big tech flips to flat or slightly down.
A last-hour swing of more than 0.5% on the S&P today is expiry flow - ignore it as a tell for Monday.
summary.confidence: low - a day-two relief rally with the gap already banked, on a quad-witching Friday; the only real volume today is in Korean memory, which the graded benchmarks barely carry.
summary.cant_know: Whether expiry flows pin or push the close. Same-day direction is close to a coin flip and I'm saying so for three of the five groups.
summary.the_call: Flat, mild. Expect the S&P and the chip index to finish within half a percent of where the pre-market has them. Big tech moves most, mildly up on the oil and yield relief; chips move least beyond their gap, because today's buying is in memory, not in the chipmakers that drive the index.
